purpose: Stone lifecycle: waiting, first touching empty craft pickup, carrying, action-byte release, throw, flight, ordered platform landing and retirement. Borrow the same physical slots for hazard contact without resetting renderer history.

inputs: Known primary or alternate stone descriptor; any word-valued slot state for the entry phase, any geometry/carried kind words, two craft records and player count.
Carry alias is player 0, or player 1 with count two. Direct attach/throw carrier is independently valid. Flight borrows up to ten platforms in original order; signed-negative left edge terminates.
outputs: Typed slot/craft mutations, contact and platform selections, transition requests. The bridge preserves the deterministic full L1 machine shell and the real synchronous throw sound ABI.
effects: No renderer-history writes. Positions/velocities and presentation sprite are committed before immediate landing initialization or sound callback.
The bridge projects fresh RAM per entry, publishes only actual stores, and uses existing phase-checked alias accessors.
preconditions: Serialized ordinary nonaliasing RAM/stack and immutable descriptor/platform inputs during one call. DS=DGROUP, CS=GAME, aligned physical slot 0..15.

Descriptor callback words must be the known stone targets. Malformed indices/identities/targets, invalid carrier aliases and unterminated platform lists use explicit L1 compatibility. No native evidence is claimed for fallback.
Native carrier arguments must be below two. Hazard views must be borrowed immediately before query in physical slot order, and hazard bounce writes returned before the next actor step.

callers: DispatchActorUpdates in ascending active-prefix order; loader bootstrap, stone descriptor tails; hazards run after actor updates and before drawing.
Routine direct-entry tests retain their live input/output register shell.

indirect.classification: Known descriptor targets checked before projection; the original dispatcher retains explicit error/fallback behavior outside the contract.

owned: Actor update phase, animation offset/countdown, sprite, X32/Y32; carried alias, thrown horizontal and vertical motion; selected craft carried kind and destination icon.
borrowed: Descriptor geometry, callbacks and carried kind; platform bounds/heights; craft position/raw velocity/action low byte.
memory.aliases: Only carrier in carried phase and horizontal_step in thrown phase are read through checked alias accessors. No table widening. All six renderer-history words remain persistent and untouched, including history seeded by the pre-game demo.
memory.hazards: Primary identity only, phase thrown, nonnegative vertical step; ascending first match. Current bridge RAM is the shared synchronization boundary, not a second cached native slot array.

assumptions: One step from any admitted scalar slot state, not a proof only from initializer-reachable states.
The full bridge formal profiles abstract a successful read-only sound callback; real sound, registers and device effects are differential/integration evidence.
L0 unchanged; L0 -> L1 remains C/D. Native A/B evidence never becomes an exact ASM/C byte-match contribution.
eliminated: Ordinary native functions use typed slots, player numbers and borrowed resources; no machine addresses/registers/dispatch in native/stones.c.
Renderer history is neither reset nor derived from current position on entry.
retained: 16-bit wrapping addition/subtraction, explicit signed word comparisons and arithmetic right shift of raw craft velocities by five.
Only action low-byte bit seven releases; high byte and all action bits survive unchanged.
Inclusive X retirement at -512, right retirement at 10240, descending bottom retirement at 6144; rising Y has no bottom retirement.
Gravity adds two before sign test; inclusive old/new platform crossing and both horizontal edges, first platform wins.

Primary and alternate identities remain distinct; only primary thrown stones can hit hazards. Initializing wait leaves sprite, velocities and render history stale; retired slots keep their descriptor/order.
